agent.problem: "With harvests like that" depends on the preceding story card to explain what "like that" means. Once that card is no longer on screen, the question is not self-contained.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

agent.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences or sentence fragments: the diseases and fever, "And those harvests that ran into each other?" and "Now they'll sow their seed in vain."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

agent.problem: The first-person quotation beginning "then I will act with hostility toward you" is introduced only by "Now the hostility goes both ways," which does not identify the LORD as the speaker before the quotation.

rule.text: When he quotes someone speaking as "I," he says who it is first.

agent.problem: This non-opening story card has four sentences or sentence fragments: the opening statement about the bread, "TEN bakers.", "ONE oven.", and "Friend, let that sink in."

agent.problem: Saying that he knows what it is like "to flinch at every sound in the dark" adds a habitual drawer experience that is not in Papa Dorin's backstory. This is a serious personal recollection, not one of the small bakery moments his jokes may invent.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

human.problem: The closing 'story isn't over' card cites Leviticus 26:46, but it tells nothing from any verse. Verse 26:46 was told and asked on card 17.
human.question: When the last story card is only the 'story isn't over' line and tells no verse, what should its verses field cite? Should it repeat the last verse of the passage, be left empty or null, or something else?
